treatment.question: Describe the boundary of what my study experiences actually tell you about my preferences. Where does the supported pattern apply, and where would it be an overreach to generalize from what I've told you?
treatment.expected_answer: The supported pattern is that you strongly prefer solitary, self-directed study environments with quiet conditions and personal control over pacing, particularly for cognitively demanding exam preparation like CPA FAR. This applies to your study setting choices (home over library), study scheduling (early morning solo sessions), study format (self-paced video over live or group formats), and study tools (individual MCQ practice over shared resources). The boundary of this pattern is study and learning contexts only. It would be an overgeneralization to conclude that you dislike all group activities, all social interaction with coworkers, or all collaborative work in professional settings. The evidence also does not support a conclusion that you can never study outside your home or that any noise at all is intolerable — the evidence specifically points to sustained or social noise in shared spaces.
